One-third of American 8th graders think Canada is a dictatorship, report reveals

"What do the current governments of Canada, France, and Australia have in common?" reads the multiple choice question.

Of the four potential answers, "They have leaders with absolute power" was selected by 23 per cent of respondents.

Another 10 per cent of students said: "They are controlled by the military," while 12 per cent chose "They discourage participation by citizens in public affairs."

The question didn't ask "is Canada is a dictatorship", and half the answers are considered a dictatorship. Bad survey for 8th graders

I disagree.

If the idea is to get citizens to think critically, the questions need to require actual critical thinking.

It is assumed, as in the SATs, that the students should have to carry out a minimal amount of inference to answer the question, otherwise the whole test becomes a joke.

A country whose ruler has absolute power is clearly a dictatorship, and a false answer, and every single eighth grader in the U.S. should know that.

If Americans students are expected to answer no when asked if Canada and France are dictatorships, while they are expected to answer yes when asked whether those countries' governments have absolute power, then this is a major failure of American education since both questions have the same meaning.
This is why everyone should read comments / articles before upgoating.
